page.layout: One column of verse, set in the upper half of the page, with a fleuron below. Below it: a two-line italic motto with a Greek line beneath, then the closing word FINIS in spaced capitals, then a printer's ornament.

main_text.p: Quid! nil perpetuum cedò, Quicquid tellus habet singula lubrica? Est, semper quod, ais, manet, Est quid, quod faciem non variat suam; Est, quæ permanet, altera Constans ac stabilis, vera, creatio, Quâ Sol Justitiæ Sacer Vult signare suos, quos amat ac fovet, Per Flamen radians suum, Mortem ne videant insuper horridam, Quos divellere non queunt A' Christo Domino nec bona nec mala. Hæc non vertit imaginem, Quæ cras,est hodie, cuncta ruant licet, Nunquàm non eadem stat hæc; Fiet terra polus, nix prius atra erit, Ante agnus comedet lupum, Ullis viribus hæc quàm detur irrita. Hem! quis doctus hic HALLER est? Dignus qui reliquas exeat ad Scholas.

p.i: Hoc amicitiæ non intermoritura πυμήνειον[?] annectere voluit, cujus

page.notes: The faint ghost text at lower left ("Quid") and the faint text in the right margin are show-through from the other side of the leaf and are left out. The Greek word in the italic motto is not clearly legible; the reading πυμήνειον is a best guess. The ornament at the foot is not text and is not transcribed. Line-final spacing and the comma before "est" in "cras,est" are copied as printed. The Greek line is copied from the scan as far as it can be read.
